prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1066; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officers responded to a collision at an intersection in Houston, Texas, involving a left turn. Driver 1 was turning left when the front of the vehicle struck the side of Driver 2's car, which had entered the intersection from the opposite direction. Driver 1 reported a knee injury and was seen by responding medics. The nature of the impact, with the force concentrated at the front of the vehicle, is consistent with the kind of injury described. Driver 2 gave a statement that matched the sequence of events. Two independent witnesses at the scene described the collision the same way, and scene photographs show damage that lines up with the reported impact. Officers and witnesses confirmed that a passenger was in Driver 1's vehicle at the time. Driver 1 said they live in the same household as the policyholder, and no prior damage to the vehicle was known to anyone at the scene or noted during the inspection.
